descriptions.text: Stock Certificate. The bearer of this instrument now holds one share of common stock in the Sigmund Textiles Foundry, a publicly-traded company based in the Gun-ya system within the Skull Empire and traded via the I.R.F. Last recorded value per share: 10.422 credits.

recap.text: Carl opens all seven silver Summary Judgement boxes, and each holds one gold piece, a stock certificate worth one share, and a photograph. No two certificates look alike: some are paper, one is an egg covered in writing, one is printed on glass. The first photograph shows the mother of Prince Stalwart of the Skull Empire, a young orc in a flowery dress and gaudy crown.

Carl laughs again as Donut cannot believe that anyone can scoot onto a satellite circling Venus, press a button and blow up the solar system. King Rust says its security is impenetrable and it will explode if anyone unauthorized tries to break in, but the Skull Empire builds backdoors into everything it makes, a secret his daughter announced to the whole galaxy. He tells Carl that the stock certificate he owns is losing significant value by the moment.

beats.headline: Seven shares, seven mothers
beats.text: All seven of Carl's silver Summary Judgement boxes open on the same three things: one gold piece, a stock certificate equal to one share, and a photograph. No two certificates look alike. Some are paper, one is an egg covered in writing, another is printed on glass. The first photograph is an ordinary eight by ten of a young orc in an overly flowery dress and a gaudy crown: the mother of Plaintiff #1, Prince Stalwart of the Skull Empire. Mordecai sits there with his beak open. The AI, he thinks, has just given Carl photographs of the mothers of everyone in that lawsuit.
beats.gist: Carl's seven silver boxes each hold a gold piece, a share certificate and a photograph of a mother.

beats.headline: About ten credits each
beats.text: Carl examines one: a share of common stock in the Sigmund Textiles Foundry of the Gun-ya system, within the Skull Empire, last valued at 10.422 credits. Odd, agrees Mordecai. He cannot remember what the I.R.F. stands for, only that it is about the biggest stock exchange in the universe, and crawlers are not even allowed to gamble at the Desperado Club's credit tables. Each certificate is from a company based in a plaintiff's system, as if the AI is needling them. The photographs are valuable too: Carl now knows the seven factions who tried to take the gate from him.
beats.gist: Carl examines seven stock certificates, odd ones from plaintiffs' home systems, and the photographs name seven factions.

beats.headline: Losing value by the moment
beats.text: Donut cannot believe that anyone can scoot onto a satellite circling Venus, press a button and blow up the solar system. Its security is impenetrable, King Rust says, and it will explode if anyone unauthorized tries to break in. But the Skull Empire manufactures the satellites, and builds backdoors into everything it makes so none of it can be used against it. That was a secret until his daughter announced it to the whole galaxy. I'm afraid that stock certificate you own, Carl, is losing significant value by the moment. Carl laughs again.
beats.gist: King Rust says the Skull Empire built backdoors into its satellites, so Donut's stock certificate loses value.
